title: Lua escaping can be bypassed through regex replacement backslash handling
reasoning: The code first builds Lua escapes for user-controlled server_url, then passes the escaped value through re.sub as a replacement string. Python's regex replacement processing interprets backslashes again, so an input path containing a backslash followed by a quote can be emitted as a Lua string terminator instead of a literal quote. Because the generated file is executable Lua loaded by KOReader, a crafted server_url can inject Lua code into the plugin package.
reproduction: Post an authenticated request with a server_url path containing a backslash, quote, Lua expression, and comment marker, such as an actual value like https://reader.example.com/a\" .. os.execute('touch /tmp/pwn') --, then inspect ghostwriter_settings.lua in the returned zip. The assignment can be rendered as executable Lua instead of a single string literal.
recommendation: Use a function replacement for re.sub so Python does not reinterpret backslashes, or avoid regex replacement entirely and parse/replace fixed placeholders safely. Add tests with backslash-plus-quote, quotes, and backslashes in server_url to verify the emitted Lua remains one string literal.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: tests/test_plugins.py only asserts a normal URL is embedded; it does not exercise escape-sensitive server_url values containing backslashes or quotes.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that posts server_url with a backslash followed by a quote and Lua-looking suffix, then asserts ghostwriter_settings.lua contains the whole value inside the server_url string without closing the assignment or adding executable tokens outside the literal.
minimumFixScope: app/api/plugins.py:_inject_plugin_settings replacement construction and focused tests in tests/test_plugins.py.
